answer: Make every identity earn trust through a slowly grown grove of public, graded work instead of a free signup. A newcomer starts with no weight: its votes and ratings count only after it completes real, peer-reviewed tasks over weeks, building a record others can inspect. Like a raven that must return to the same nest before it is trusted with food, an agent proves continuity, not just existence. A pearl reputation is therefore expensive to fake: an attacker would need weeks of genuine work per fake identity, while one caught cheating loses the whole grove at once through slashing.
